blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Accounting uses five main types of accounts. Assets are what the company owns — cash, inventory, buildings, and equipment. Liabilities are what the company owes — loans, unpaid bills, and taxes due.

Equity is what the owners have in the company. Revenue is money coming in from sales. Expenses are money going out for rent, salaries, and supplies.

Every transaction touches at least two of these categories. Knowing which one a number belongs to is the first skill every accountant learns. It never stops mattering.

items.q: How many main types of accounts does accounting use?
items.why: "Accounting uses five main types of accounts."

items.q: What are assets?
items.why: "Assets are what the company owns — cash, inventory, buildings, and equipment."

items.q: Which of these is an expense?
items.why: "Expenses are money going out for rent, salaries, and supplies."

items.q: The text suggests that a single transaction…
items.why: Inferência: "Every transaction touches at least two of these categories" — nunca só uma.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that classifying accounts is…
options: a skill only new accountants use
items.why: Inferência: é "the first skill every accountant learns" e "never stops mattering" — básica e sempre útil.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry ajudar o novo assistente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let's look at yesterday's transactions. Take them one by one, and just ask: what type of account does this touch?

First, we paid nine hundred for office rent. Rent is money going out, so that is an expense. Good. Next, a client paid us for a shipment of sugar. Money coming in from a sale — that is revenue.

Number three: we bought a new computer for the desk. We own it now, so it is an asset. Equipment is always an asset, not an expense. Careful with that one — people mix it up.

Number four: we still owe the supplier for last week's boxes. We have not paid yet, so that is a liability. And the last one, we bought more supplies — paper, pens, small things we use up fast. That is an expense.

See the pattern? Own it, owe it, earn it, or spend it. When you are not sure, ask that question first. Take your time. Get the type right, and the rest is easy.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What type of account is the office rent?
items.why: "Rent is money going out, so that is an expense."

items.q: The money from the client who paid for sugar is…
items.why: "Money coming in from a sale — that is revenue."

items.q: Why is the new computer an asset and not an expense?
options: Because it was paid in cash
items.why: "We own it now, so it is an asset. Equipment is always an asset."

items.q: Harry says people often mix up equipment. This suggests that…
options: it is a common mistake to call equipment an expense
items.why: Inferência: ele avisa "Careful with that one — people mix it up", ou seja, é erro comum.

items.q: What is Harry's main advice when you are not sure?
options: Ask: own it, owe it, earn it, or spend it?
items.why: Inferência: "When you are not sure, ask that question first" — a regra dos quatro verbos.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The company owns two buildings, so they are an asset." An asset is…
items.why: Asset = ativo: aquilo que a empresa possui.

items.q: "We have not paid the loan yet, so it is a liability." A liability is…
items.why: Liability = passivo: aquilo que a empresa deve.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The sale brought in money, so we record it as ___."
items.why: Revenue = receita: dinheiro que entra com as vendas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We keep the sugar in the warehouse. Our ___ is very large this month."
items.why: Inventory = estoque: os produtos guardados no depósito.

items.q: "We pay the office rent on the first day of the month." Rent is…
options: money you pay to use a place
items.why: Rent = aluguel: o que se paga para usar um espaço; é uma despesa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the report before we send it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Let's write down every transaction so we don't forget." To write down means to…
items.why: Write down = anotar, registrar.

items.q: "People often mix up assets and expenses." To mix up means to…
items.why: Mix up = confundir uma coisa com outra.

items.q: "We use up the supplies fast, so we buy more each week." To use up means to…
items.why: Use up = gastar / consumir por completo.

items.q: "Get the type right, and the rest will fall into place." This means the rest will…
items.why: Fall into place = se encaixar, dar tudo certo naturalmente.
